prompt_text: I need a dental implant in Charlotte. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Charlotte for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
Do you mean Charlotte, NC? If so I can make a short list of nearby offices for you — I don’t have live web access in this chat, so if you want a verified, up‑to‑date list please tell me your ZIP or neighborhood and I’ll tell you exactly what to search for and what to ask. Meanwhile, here’s a practical, immediately useful answer.

Which practices to call (and why)
- Board‑certified oral & maxillofacial surgery offices
  - Why: these surgeons place implants routinely, handle complex extractions, bone grafting and sinus lifts, and offer IV sedation/general anesthesia when needed. Good for medically complex cases and multi‑implant/full‑arch cases.
- Periodontists (gum specialists who place implants)
  - Why: strong expertise in bone and soft‑tissue management (grafts, esthetic gum results) and long‑term implant maintenance.
- Prosthodontists (restorative specialists)
  - Why: best for planning and restoring implants (crowns, bridges, full‑arch prostheses) when esthetics, bite, or full‑mouth rehab are important.
- Implant‑focused dental centers (multi‑disciplinary teams)
  - Why: coordinate surgeon + restorative dentist in one practice; often offer CBCT imaging and guided implant workflows.
- Academic or hospital‑affiliated dental/oral surgery clinics
  - Why: access to experienced faculty, sometimes lower fees; good option if you want a thorough consult or a complex case managed by a team.

How to find trustworthy local practices
- Use AAOMS (American Association of Oral & Maxillofacial Surgeons) directory for oral surgeons.
- Use AAID (American Academy of Implant Dentistry) and AAP (American Academy of Periodontology) directories for implant dentists/periodontists.
- Search Google Maps for “oral surgeon Charlotte NC”, “periodontist Charlotte NC”, “implant dentist Charlotte NC” and read recent patient reviews; prefer practices with many recent 4–5 star reviews and before/after photos.
- Check whether the surgeon is board certified (oral surgeons) or a Diplomate of recognized implant organizations.

What to ask when you call (quick script)
- “Do you do dental implant placement in‑house, or do you refer the restoration to another dentist?”
- “Do you use CBCT 3‑D imaging for implant planning?”
- “What implant systems/brands do you use?”
- “Is guided (computer‑planned) implant placement available?”
- “How many implants do you place per year? Do you have experience with [single implant / bone grafting / sinus lift / full‑arch/all‑on‑4]?”
- “What are the estimated fees (surgery, implant fixture, abutment, crown) and payment/financing options?”
- “Do you offer sedation (oral/IV) and what are the pre/post‑op instructions?”
- “Can you share before/after photos and patient references or reviews?”
- “What is the expected timeline from placement to final crown?”

Typical cost and timeline (ballpark)
- Single implant (surgery + implant fixture): approximately $1,500–$3,000+
- Abutment + crown/restoration: $800–$2,500+ (varies with crown material)
- Bone grafting/sinus lift (if needed): $300–$3,000+
- Timeline: 3–6 months for typical placement → osseointegration → crown; immediate‑load options exist for eligible cases.

Next step I can do for you
- If you give me your Charlotte ZIP or neighborhood and say whether you prefer hospital‑affiliated, a short drive, or a specific budget/insurance, I’ll list 4–6 specific local oral surgeons, periodontists, and implant centers to call and give a prioritized short reason for each (experience, technology, sedation options, restorative coordination).
